summary: Today’s pulse tracks Self-driving cars should be taxed to offset job losses, thinktank urges, Mail on Sunday ends up funding state school scholarship via payout to MP, and Trump uses 9/11 memorial speech to defend Iran war as families commemorate victims of attack – live. Across Guardian and BBC, the strongest repeated signals are september, catherine, and president. In the background, Remembrance ceremonies held across the US to honor victims of 9/11 and How global trade and oil prices could be hit by Houthi advance keep the wider picture in motion.

headlines.title: Self-driving cars should be taxed to offset job losses, thinktank urges
headlines.description: Report warns widespread autonomous vehicle adoption would put hundreds of thousands of private hire jobs at risk Taxes on self-driving cars should be introduced now in the UK to offset the rise in congestion and threats to jobs they pose, a thinktank has urged. The first robotaxis on London’s streets only started this month , but government projections are that up to 40% of cars sold could be capable of self-driving capability by the middle of the next decade.

headlines.title: Mail on Sunday ends up funding state school scholarship via payout to MP
headlines.description: Labour’s Catherine Atkinson says she will give students £5,000 paid to her by paper that falsely accused her of concealing private school education A new scholarship supporting state-educated students will be inadvertently funded by the Mail on Sunday, using a payout it made after being threatened with legal action by the Labour MP Catherine Atkinson. The Derby North MP says she will use the proceeds of around £5,000 from the Mail on Sunday (MoS) to fund scholarships for local law students at the University of Derby who – like her – attended state schools.

headlines.title: Trump uses 9/11 memorial speech to defend Iran war as families commemorate victims of attack – live
headlines.description: President appears to tie Iran war to ‘sacred oath’ to victims killed in September 11 attacks as memorials are held across the US On 11 September, 25 years ago, Osama bin Laden drove with a small number of al-Qaida retainers and aides to a remote location in eastern Afghanistan. His convoy of SUVs was accompanied by a minivan converted into a makeshift communications centre. The van’s rudimentary equipment did not allow Bin Laden to watch the 19 men he had started sending to the US more than a year before fly planes into the twin towers in New York and the Pentagon near Washington DC, killing about 3,000 people. But he listened as shocked radio announcers broke the news.

headlines.title: Remembrance ceremonies held across the US to honor victims of 9/11
headlines.description: Memorials and remembrances mark the 25 years since the attacks that killed nearly 3,000 on 11 September 2001 US marks 25 years since 9/11 – latest updates The United States marked the 25th anniversary of the September 11 terrorist attacks on Friday, with memorials and remembrance ceremonies taking place across the country to honor the nearly 3,000 people killed. In New York City , the National September 11 Memorial & Museum’s annual commemoration ceremony began early on Friday morning in lower Manhattan at the site often known as Ground Zero after the destruction of the World Trade Center there on 9/11.

headlines.title: How global trade and oil prices could be hit by Houthi advance
headlines.description: Yemen's Houthis have seized territory near the Bab al-Mandab Strait - a key trade gateway for oil and global shipping.

headlines.title: Ireland holds its breath as its leftwing president prepares to meet Trump
headlines.description: Many are rooting for vocal critic Catherine Connolly to let rip in Dublin meeting, but others hope she holds back Ireland’s president, Catherine Connolly, has called Donald Trump abhorrent and an abuser of power. In his sole previous comment on Connolly, the US president seemed to think she was a man. Now that they are about to meet, Ireland is holding its breath. Trump is to fly into Dublin on Saturday morning for a two-day visit centred on golf. But before making it to his beloved greens, protocol obliges him to meet a woman who has given every impression of loathing him.

headlinePool.title: UK man pleads guilty to sexual crimes against another man’s unconscious wife
headlinePool.description: Darren Conway admits 11 charges after the Met identified him as a member of an online sexual offending forum A man has admitted using an online sexual abuse network to commit a host of sexual crimes, along with another man, against the latter’s unconscious wife. Darren Conway, 52, pleaded guilty to 11 charges at Wood Green crown court. They included voyeurism, possession of extreme pornography and encouraging the other man to sexually abuse his wife on Conway’s behalf.

headlinePool.title: Norway's Princess Astrid dies two days after attending brother King Harald's funeral
headlinePool.description: Princess Astrid "represented the Royal House in a warm and dutiful manner", the new king, Haakon VIII, said in a tribute to his aunt.

headlinePool.title: MPs reject assisted dying bill after tense debate – as it happened
headlinePool.description: The bill would have allowed terminally ill adults with less than six months to live to end their lives, after the approval of a panel of experts MPs vote against legalising assisted dying in England and Wales While the debate continues, we have a comment from Sam Royston, executive director of research and policy at Marie Curie . He said the government must address the crisis in palliative care regardless of what happens with assisted dying, calling for a new framework and funding to ensure everyone has access to compassionate end-of-life care. He said: Whatever happens with assisted dying, the UK government must fix the crisis in palliative care. It is devastating that nearly one in three people die without the help they need. Too many spend their final days in pain or on busy, chaotic hospital wards, while families are left fighting for help instead of spending time with the people they love. I think it’s absolutely right that, for instance, the prime minister and the government have said that improving palliative care must be a priority for him and his government. I think that’s something that we can all support. I think everybody should have access to good quality palliative and hospice end-of-life care at their final moment.”

headlinePool.title: US lettuce prices chopped as costs for other goods remain stubbornly high
headlinePool.description: Price for the crop dropped dramatically this summer after the cyclospora outbreak caused demand to wilt At the Republicans’ midterm convention held earlier this week, Donald Trump said that “food prices and almost every other item are rapidly going down”. Fresh inflation data on Friday told a different story – but in one specific case, costs have been chopped. The price of lettuce dropped dramatically this summer after the cyclospora outbreak caused demand to wilt, with prices dropping even further in August, according to new data released on Friday.

headlinePool.title: Extra fishy: your tinned mackerel may not be what you think it is
headlinePool.description: Substitution with jack mackerel, a different species, because of dwindling stocks is criticised by the consumer group Which? If you’ve recently opened a tin of mackerel and thought there was something fishy going on, you may have been right. An overfishing crisis means that instead of traditional mackerel, some now contain a different fish with a similar name, prompting concerns that shoppers are being short-changed. Over the past year big brands such as Princes, as well as some supermarket own-labels, have replaced traditional tinned mackerel fillets with jack mackerel fillets.

headlinePool.title: Iran’s Houthi allies capture strategic island on vital oil shipping route
headlinePool.description: Rampant Yemeni fighters take control of island in narrow point of Bab al-Mandab strait, which Saudi is relying on for oil exports Violence in Yemen: why it matters and how it is linked to the US-Iran war Yemen’s rampant Houthi forces have captured the strategic island of Perim in the Bab al-Mandab strait, expanding their control of the narrow waterway, one of the ​world’s vital shipping routes. The Iran-aligned Houthis took control of the volcanic island after forces allied to the UN-backed, Aden-based government left in the latest of a dramatic series of reverses along Yemen’s west coast in recent days, including the loss of the port city of Mocha on Thursday.

headlinePool.title: Israel says it has destroyed major underground Hezbollah base
headlinePool.description: The powerful blast registered as the equivalent of a magnitude 4.1 earthquake, according to the US Geological Survey.

headlinePool.title: AfD’s new state MPs include ex-Stasi officer, former porn actor, neopagans and neo-Nazis
headlinePool.description: Far-right German party’s newly elected representatives face fresh scrutiny as it tries to form government in Saxony-Anhalt • Why is the AfD’s state victory significant and what might happen next? The Alternative für Deutschland is facing scrutiny over the suitability of some of its prospective new MPs – including a former Stasi officer and a former pornography actor – just days after its historic win in the German state of Saxony-Anhalt . Presented by the AfD’s lead candidate, Ulrich Siegmund, for a photocall in the state capital of Magdeburg on Thursday, some of the members-elect were revealed to have a range of questionable backgrounds, including criminal records, Stasi pasts and connections to far-right networks.

headlinePool.title: As diseases loom, CDC's response to measles deaths stirs fears about agency's reliability
headlinePool.description: The worst U.S. measles outbreak in decades is growing and flu season is imminent. Experts are fretting about federal health data reliability after the CDC questioned two Pennsylvania measles deaths.
